title.zh: 卷二十六 唐臣傳第十四: 符習 烏震 孔謙 張延朗 李嚴 李仁矩 毛璋
title.en: Volume 26 Later Tang Biographies 6: Fu Xi, Wu Zhen, Kong Qian, Zhang Yanlang, Li Yan, Li Renju, Mao Zhang
title.raw: 卷二十六 唐臣傳第十四: 符習 烏震 孔謙 張延朗 李嚴 李仁矩 毛璋 Volume 26 Later Tang Biographies 6: Fu Xi, Wu Zhen, Kong Qian, Zhang Yanlang, Li Yan, Li Renju, Mao Zhang

sentences.zh: 符習，趙州昭慶人也。

translations.literal: Fu Xi was a native of Zhaqing in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi came from Zhaqing in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少事趙王王镕為軍校，自晉救趙，破梁軍柏鄉，趙常遣習將兵從晉。

translations.literal: As a youth he served the Zhao king Wang Rong as a military officer; he joined Jin in rescuing Zhao, broke Liang forces at Baixiang, and Zhao often sent Xi leading troops to follow Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Wang Rong of Zhao as a military officer. When Jin marched to save Zhao and broke Liang at Baixiang, Zhao often sent Xi with Jin’s host.

sentences.zh: 晉軍德勝，張文禮弒趙王王镕，上書莊宗，求習歸趙。

translations.literal: Jin’s army won at Desheng; Zhang Wenli assassinated the Zhao king Wang Rong and wrote to Zhuangzong requesting Xi be sent back to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin’s victory at Desheng, Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong of Zhao and petitioned Zhuangzong to send Xi home to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣之，習號泣曰：「臣世家趙，受趙王恩，王嘗以一劍與臣使自效，今聞王死，欲以劍自裁，念卒無益，請擊趙破賊，報王冤。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent him; Xi wept aloud and said: “My family has served Zhao for generations; I received the Zhao king’s grace. The king once gave me a sword to serve with my life. Now that I hear the king is dead, I wish to use that sword on myself—but that would serve nothing in the end. I ask to strike Zhao, break the rebels, and avenge the king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent him off. Xi wept and said: “My house has served Zhao for generations, and the king once gave me a sword to spend my life in his service. Now that he is dead I mean to fall on that sword—but what good would that do? Let me strike Zhao, break the rebels, and avenge my king.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗壯之，乃遣閻寶、史建瑭等助習討文禮，以習為鎮州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was impressed, then sent Yan Bao, Shi Jiantan, and others to help Xi suppress Wenli, and made Xi acting regional commander of Zhenzhou horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong was moved. He sent Yan Bao and Shi Jiantan to help Xi crush Wenli and made Xi acting commander of Zhenzhou’s forces.

sentences.zh: 習攻文禮不克，莊宗用佗將破之。

translations.literal: Xi attacked Wenli but could not overcome him; Zhuangzong used other generals to break him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi besieged Wenli without success; Zhuangzong sent other commanders and broke him.

sentences.zh: 拜習成德軍節度使，習辭不敢受，乃以相、衛二州為義寧軍，以習為節度使，習辭曰：「魏博六州，霸王之府也，不宜分割以示弱，願授臣河南一鎮，得自攻取之。

translations.literal: Xi was appointed military governor of the Chengde army; Xi declined, not daring to accept. They then made Xiang and Wei prefectures into the Yining army and appointed Xi its military governor. Xi declined, saying: “The six prefectures of Weibo are the seat of a hegemon—they should not be carved up to show weakness. Grant me one command south of the Yellow River, and I will take it myself.
translations.idiomatic: They offered Xi the Chengde command; he refused. They carved Xiang and Wei into the Yining army and made him its governor. He refused again: “Weibo’s six prefectures are a hegemon’s seat—split them and you look weak. Give me one command south of the river and I will win it myself.

sentences.zh: 」乃拜習天平軍節度使、東南面招討使，習亦未嘗攻取。

translations.literal: ” He was then appointed military governor of the Tianping army and southeast pacification commissioner; Xi also never actually attacked and seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: ” They made him military governor of Tianping and southeast pacification commissioner—but he never took a command by force.

sentences.zh: 後徙鎮安國，又徙平盧。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to command An’guo, then transferred again to Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved to An’guo, then to Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮作亂，遣習以鎮兵討賊。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, they sent Xi with his garrison troops to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rose in rebellion, Xi was sent with his garrison to put him down.

sentences.zh: 習未至魏，而明宗兵變，習不敢進。

translations.literal: Xi had not yet reached Wei when Mingzong’s troops mutinied; Xi dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xi reached Wei, Mingzong’s army turned on him. Xi halted and would not go on.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣人招之，習見明宗於胙縣，而以明宗舉兵不順，去就之意未決，霍彥威紿習曰：「主上所殺者十人，公居其四，復何猶豫乎？

translations.literal: Mingzong sent men to summon him; Xi met Mingzong at Zuo county. Because Mingzong’s raising of troops was improper, his mind on whether to stay or leave was still unsettled. Huo Yanwei deceived Xi, saying: “Of the ten men the emperor killed, you were four—why still hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent for him. Xi met him at Zuo county, but Mingzong’s rebellion still left him torn. Huo Yanwei lied to him: “The emperor killed ten men—and you were four of them. What is there to hesitate over?

sentences.zh: 」習意乃決。

translations.literal: ” Xi’s mind was made up.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xi made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 平盧監軍楊希望聞習為明宗所召，乃以兵圍習家屬，將殺之。

translations.literal: The Pinglu army monitor Yang Xiwang heard Xi had been summoned by Mingzong and surrounded Xi’s family with troops, about to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiwang, the Pinglu army monitor, heard Xi had gone over to Mingzong. He surrounded Xi’s family with troops and meant to kill them.

sentences.zh: 指揮使王公儼素為希望所信，紿希望曰：「內侍盡忠朝廷，誅反者家族，孰敢不效命！

translations.literal: The commander Wang Gongyan had long been trusted by Xiwang; he deceived Xiwang, saying: “The inner attendant is wholly loyal to the court in punishing rebel families—who would not obey!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongyan, a commander Xiwang trusted, tricked him: “You serve the throne faithfully by destroying a rebel’s kin—who would not follow you?

sentences.zh: 宜分兵守城，以虞外變，習家不足慮也。

translations.literal: You should divide your troops to guard the city and guard against outside changes; Xi’s family is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Split your force and hold the walls against trouble outside. Xi’s family is no concern.

sentences.zh: 」希望信之，乃悉分其兵守城，公儼因擒希望斬之，習家屬由是獲免。

translations.literal: ” Xiwang believed him, divided all his troops to guard the city, and Gongyan thereby captured Xiwang and executed him; Xi’s family thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xiwang believed him and sent his men to the walls. Gongyan seized him and cut off his head. Xi’s family was spared.

sentences.zh: 而公儼宣言青人不便習之嚴急，不欲習復來，因自求為節度使。

translations.literal: Gongyan then proclaimed that the people of Qing province could not bear Xi’s harsh severity and did not want Xi to return; he therefore sought the military governorship for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyan then declared that Qing’s people hated Xi’s harsh rule and would not have him back—and asked for the command himself.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃以房知溫代習鎮平盧，拜公儼登州刺史。

translations.literal: Mingzong then had Fang Zhiwen replace Xi at Pinglu and appointed Gongyan prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong replaced Xi with Fang Zhiwen at Pinglu and made Gongyan prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 公儼不時承命，知溫擒而殺之。

translations.literal: Gongyan did not promptly obey; Zhiwen captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyan would not obey. Zhiwen took him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 習復鎮天平，徙鎮宣武。

translations.literal: Xi again commanded Tianping, then was transferred to command Xuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi returned to Tianping, then moved to Xuanyu.

sentences.zh: 習素為安重誨所不悅，希其旨者上言習厚斂汴人，乃以太子太師致仕，歸昭慶故里，明宗以其子令謙為趙州刺史以奉養之。

translations.literal: Xi had long been disliked by An Chonghui; those hoping to please Chonghui memorialized that Xi heavily taxed the people of Bian. He was therefore made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired, returning to his homeland in Zhaqing. Mingzong made his son Lingqian prefect of Zhao to support him.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui had never liked Xi. Men eager to please Chonghui accused him of bleeding Bian dry. Xi was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and sent home to Zhaqing. Mingzong made his son Lingqian prefect of Zhao to provide for him.

sentences.zh: 習以無罪，怏怏失職，縱獵劇飲以自娛。

translations.literal: Xi, believing himself without guilt, was resentful at losing his post and hunted and drank heavily for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Innocent in his own eyes, Xi brooded over his fall and drowned his days in hunting and wine.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，中風卒，贈太師。

translations.literal: After slightly more than a year he suffered a stroke and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he suffered a stroke and died. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 習二子：令謙、蒙。

translations.literal: Xi had two sons: Lingqian and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had two sons: Lingqian and Meng.

sentences.zh: 令謙有勇力，善騎射，以父任為將，官至趙州刺史，有善政，卒於州，州人號泣送葬者數千人，當時號為良刺史。

translations.literal: Lingqian had courage and strength and was skilled at mounted archery; through his father’s position he served as a general, reached the office of Zhao prefect, and governed well. He died in office; people of the prefecture wept at his burial, numbering several thousand. At the time he was called an excellent prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqian was strong, brave, and a fine mounted archer. His father’s rank made him a general; he rose to prefect of Zhao and ruled well. He died in office, and thousands wept at his funeral. Men called him a model prefect.

sentences.zh: 蒙少好學，性剛鯁，為成德軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Meng in youth loved learning; his nature was stubborn and upright. He served as deputy military governor of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Meng loved books as a boy and was stiff-necked by nature. He became deputy military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 後事晉，官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served Jin and reached the office of Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Jin and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 烏震，冀州信都人也。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen was a native of Xindu in Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen came from Xindu in Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少事趙王王镕為軍卒，稍以功遷裨校，隸符習軍。

translations.literal: As a youth he served the Zhao king Wang Rong as a soldier, was gradually promoted to captain through merit, and was attached to Fu Xi’s army.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Wang Rong of Zhao as a common soldier, won promotion to captain, and joined Fu Xi’s command.

sentences.zh: 習從莊宗於河上，而镕為張文禮所弒，震從習討文禮，而家在趙，文禮執震母妻及子十餘人以招震，震不顧。

translations.literal: Xi followed Zhuangzong on the river; Rong was assassinated by Zhang Wenli. Zhen followed Xi against Wenli, but his family was in Zhao. Wenli seized Zhen’s mother, wife, and more than ten children to lure Zhen; Zhen paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Xi followed Zhuangzong on the river while Wenli murdered Wang Rong. Zhen marched with Xi against Wenli, but his kin were still in Zhao. Wenli seized Zhen’s mother, wife, and more than ten children to force him over. Zhen would not look.

sentences.zh: 文禮乃皆斷其手鼻，割而不誅，縱至習軍，軍中皆不忍正視。

translations.literal: Wenli then cut off all their hands and noses, mutilated but did not kill them, and released them to Xi’s army. Everyone in the army could not bear to look directly.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli cut off their hands and noses, maimed but did not kill them, and sent them to Xi’s camp. No soldier could meet their eyes.

sentences.zh: 震一慟而止，憤激自勵，身先士卒。

translations.literal: Zhen grieved once and stopped; stirred by indignation he steeled himself and led from the front among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wept once, then checked himself. Shame hardened him; he took the van and fought at the head of the line.

sentences.zh: 晉軍攻破鎮州，震以功拜刺史，歷深、趙二州。

translations.literal: Jin’s army broke Zhenzhou; Zhen through merit was appointed prefect and served successively at Deep and Zhao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin broke Zhenzhou, Zhen won a prefecture for his deeds and served at Deep and Zhao in turn.

sentences.zh: 震為人純質，少好學，通《左氏春秋》，喜作詩，善書。

translations.literal: Zhen as a person was plain and sincere; in youth he loved learning, mastered the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, enjoyed writing poetry, and was skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was plain and honest. As a young man he studied the Zuo Commentary, wrote verse, and practiced calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 及為刺史，以廉平為政有聲，遷冀州刺史，兼北面水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When he became prefect he governed with integrity and fairness and won renown; he was transferred to Ji prefecture and concurrently made north water-and-land transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he ruled with clean hands and a fair scale and won a name for it. He became prefect of Ji and north water-and-land transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明宗聞其名，擢拜河北道副招討使，領寧國軍節度使，代房知溫戍於盧臺軍。

translations.literal: Mingzong heard his name, promoted him to deputy Hebei pacification commissioner, made him military governor of the Ningguo army, and had him replace Fang Zhiwen garrisoning at Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong heard of him, made him deputy Hebei pacification commissioner and military governor of Ningguo, and sent him to Lutai in Fang Zhiwen’s place.

sentences.zh: 始至而戍兵龍至等作亂，見殺，贈太師。

translations.literal: He had just arrived when garrison soldiers Long Zhi and others rebelled; he was killed. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely arrived when Long Zhi and other garrison troops mutinied and killed him. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 忠孝以義則兩得，吾既已言之矣，若烏震者，可謂忠乎？

translations.literal: With loyalty and filial piety, by righteousness both may be obtained—I have already said this. As for one like Wu Zhen, can he be called loyal?
translations.idiomatic: By righteousness, loyalty and filial piety can both be kept—I have said as much already. But can a man like Wu Zhen be called loyal?

sentences.zh: 甚矣，震之不思也。

translations.literal: How greatly Wu Zhen failed to think!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen did not think at all.

sentences.zh: 夫食人之祿而任人之事，事有任，專其責，而其國之利害，由己之為不為，為之雖利於國，而有害於其親者，猶將辭其祿而去之。

translations.literal: To eat another’s salary and undertake another’s task: when a task is assigned, one’s responsibility is fixed, and the benefit or harm to the state depends on whether one acts or not. Even if acting benefits the state but harms one’s kin, one should still resign the salary and leave.
translations.idiomatic: A man who eats another’s salary and bears another’s charge owns a fixed duty. The state rises or falls on what he does or refuses to do. Even when action helps the realm but hurts his kin, he should give up rank and go.

sentences.zh: 矧其事眾人所皆可為，而任不專己，又其為與不為，國之利害不系焉者，如是而不顧其親，雖不以為利，猶曰不孝，況因而利之乎！

translations.literal: How much more when the task is what everyone could do, responsibility is not solely one’s own, and whether one acts or not does not affect the state’s benefit or harm! To ignore one’s kin in such a case—even if not for profit—is still called unfilial; how much more when profit comes from it!
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when anyone could do the work, the charge is not yours alone, and the realm’s fate does not hang on your choice! To abandon your kin even then is already unfilial—what name is left when you do it for gain?

sentences.zh: 夫能事其親以孝，然後能事其君以忠，若烏震者，可謂大不孝矣，尚何有於忠哉！

translations.literal: Only one who can serve his kin with filial piety can then serve his lord with loyalty. As for Wu Zhen, he may be called greatly unfilial—what then remains of loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Only a filial son can be a loyal minister. Wu Zhen was deeply unfilial—what loyalty could he claim?

sentences.zh: 孔謙，魏州人也，為魏州孔目官。

translations.literal: Kong Qian was a native of Weizhou and served as a Weizhou clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian came from Weizhou and served as a clerical officer there.

sentences.zh: 魏博入於晉，莊宗以為度支使。

translations.literal: When Weibo entered Jin, Zhuangzong made him fiscal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Weibo submitted to Jin, Zhuangzong made him fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 謙為人勤敏，而傾巧善事人，莊宗及其左右皆悅之。

translations.literal: Qian was diligent and clever by nature, but clever in scheming and good at pleasing people; Zhuangzong and those around him all liked him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was quick and clever, slick at pleasing men. Zhuangzong and his court liked him.

sentences.zh: 自少為吏，工書算，頗知金谷聚斂之事。

translations.literal: From youth as a clerk he was skilled at writing and calculation and knew much about finance and revenue collection.
translations.idiomatic: Raised as a clerk, he was skilled at ledgers and knew how to squeeze the treasury.

sentences.zh: 晉與梁相拒河上十餘年，大小百餘戰，謙調發供饋，未嘗闕乏，所以成莊宗之業者，謙之力為多，然民亦不勝其苦也。

translations.literal: Jin and Liang opposed each other on the river for more than ten years in over a hundred battles large and small. Qian managed mobilization and supplies and never fell short; that Zhuangzong’s enterprise succeeded owed much to Qian’s power—yet the people also could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years Jin and Liang fought on the river in a hundred battles, large and small. Qian kept the levies and the grain flowing and never failed Zhuangzong’s cause—but the people groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初建大號，謙自謂當為租庸使，而郭崇韜用魏博觀察使判官張憲為使，以謙為副。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first established the great title, Qian assumed he would become grain-and-corvée commissioner; but Guo Chongtao used Weibo observation commissioner’s secretary Zhang Xian as commissioner, with Qian as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the imperial title, Qian expected to become grain-and-corvée commissioner. Guo Chongtao instead made Zhang Xian, secretary to the Weibo observation commissioner, commissioner—with Qian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 謙已怏怏。

translations.literal: Qian was already discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was already bitter.

sentences.zh: 既而莊宗滅梁，謙從入汴，謂崇韜曰：「鄴，北都也，宜得重人鎮之，非張憲不可。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qian followed him into Bian and told Chongtao: “Ye is the northern capital—it should have a weighty man to command it. None but Zhang Xian will do.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Bian, Qian told Chongtao: “Ye is the northern capital and needs a heavy hand. Only Zhang Xian will do.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜以為然，因以憲留守北都，而以宰相豆盧革判租庸。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao thought it so, therefore had Xian remain at the northern capital and had the chief minister Dou Lu’ge judge grain-and-corvée affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao agreed. He left Xian at the northern capital and put Chief Minister Dou Lu’ge over grain and corvée.

sentences.zh: 謙益失望，乃陰求革過失，而革嘗以手書假租庸錢十萬，謙因以書示崇韜，而微泄其事，使革聞之。

translations.literal: Qian grew more disappointed and secretly sought Ge’s faults. Ge had once borrowed grain-and-corvée funds of one hundred thousand in his own hand; Qian showed the letter to Chongtao and slightly leaked the matter, letting Ge hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian grew more disappointed and hunted for Ge’s faults. Ge had once borrowed a hundred thousand in grain funds in his own hand. Qian showed the note to Chongtao and let the story leak until Ge heard it.

sentences.zh: 革懼，遂求解職以讓崇韜，崇韜亦不肯當。

translations.literal: Ge was afraid and requested to resign to yield to Chongtao; Chongtao also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was frightened and offered to step aside for Chongtao. Chongtao would not take the post either.

sentences.zh: 莊宗問：「誰可者？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong asked: “Who is suitable?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong asked, “Who should have it?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜曰：「孔謙雖長於金谷，而物議未可居大任，不若復用張憲。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao said: “Though Kong Qian excels at finance, public opinion says he cannot hold great responsibility—better to reuse Zhang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao said, “Kong Qian knows the ledgers, but men say he is unfit for high office. Better to recall Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 」乃趣召憲。

translations.literal: ” They then urgently summoned Xian.
translations.idiomatic: ” They hurried a summons to Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲為人明辯，人頗忌之，謙因乘間謂革曰：「租庸錢谷，悉在目前，委一小吏可辦。

translations.literal: Xian as a person was clear and argumentative; people greatly resented him. Qian took the opportunity to tell Ge: “Grain-and-corvée funds and grain are all before our eyes—a minor clerk could handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was sharp-tongued and clear-minded, and many resented him. Qian seized the moment and told Ge, “The grain money is all here in the office. A petty clerk could run it.

sentences.zh: 鄴都天下之重，不可輕以任人。

translations.literal: Ye capital is the weight of the realm—it cannot lightly be given to anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Ye is the weight of the empire. You cannot put it in the wrong hands.

sentences.zh: 」革以語崇韜，崇韜罷憲不召，以興唐尹王正言為租庸使。

translations.literal: ” Ge told this to Chongtao; Chongtao dismissed summoning Xian and made Xingtang governor Wang Zhengyan grain-and-corvée commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ge repeated this to Chongtao. Chongtao dropped the recall and made Xingtang governor Wang Zhengyan grain-and-corvée commissioner.

sentences.zh: 謙益憤憤，因求解職。

translations.literal: Qian grew more resentful and requested to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Qian grew angrier still and asked to quit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒其避事，欲寘之法，賴伶官景進救解之，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry at his shirking duties and wanted to punish him by law; only the eunuch-official Jing Jin’s intercession saved him, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged at his shirking and meant to punish him by law. Only Jing Jin, the eunuch-official, talked him out of it.

sentences.zh: 已而正言病風，不任事，景進數以為言，乃罷正言，以謙為租庸使，賜「豐財贍國功臣」。

translations.literal: Soon Zhengyan suffered a stroke and could not handle affairs; Jing Jin several times spoke on it. They then dismissed Zhengyan, made Qian grain-and-corvée commissioner, and granted him the title “Meritorious in Enriching Wealth and Nourishing the State.”
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhengyan was struck with paralysis and could not serve. Jing Jin kept pressing the point. Zhengyan was removed, Qian got the commission, and the throne gave him the title Meritorious in Enriching Wealth and Nourishing the State.

sentences.zh: 謙無佗能，直以聚斂為事。

translations.literal: Qian had no other ability; he simply made revenue collection his business.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had no other gift. He lived to squeeze.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初即位，推恩天下，除百姓田租，放諸場務課利欠負者，謙悉違詔督理。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first took the throne he extended grace to the realm, cancelled the people’s land tax, and released debts owed from various market taxes and profits. Qian entirely disobeyed the edict and enforced collection.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first ascended he cancelled land tax and wiped market debts across the realm. Qian ignored every word and kept collecting.

sentences.zh: 故事：觀察使所治屬州事，皆不得奪達，上所賦調，亦下觀察使行之。

translations.literal: Former custom: what observation commissioners governed regarding subordinate prefectures none could preempt by direct transmission; what the emperor assigned for levy also went down through observation commissioners to implement.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, observation commissioners controlled their subordinate prefectures and no one could bypass them. Imperial levies also passed through them.

sentences.zh: 而謙直以租庸帖調發諸州，不關觀察，觀察使交章論理，以謂：「制敕不下支郡，刺史不專奏事，唐制也。

translations.literal: But Qian directly used grain-and-corvée posts to mobilize from various prefectures without involving observation commissioners. Observation commissioners sent joint memorials arguing, saying: “Edicts do not go down to branch prefectures; prefects do not solely memorialize—the Tang system.
translations.idiomatic: Qian instead issued grain-and-corvée orders straight to the prefectures, cutting observation commissioners out. They protested in joint memorials: “Edicts do not go to branch prefectures, and prefects do not memorialize on their own—that is Tang law.

sentences.zh: 租庸直帖，沿偽梁之弊，不可為法。

translations.literal: Direct grain-and-corvée posts follow the corrupt practice of false Liang and cannot serve as law.
translations.idiomatic: Direct grain posts copy false Liang’s abuse and must not become precedent.

sentences.zh: 今唐運中興，願還舊制。

translations.literal: Now Tang’s fortune rises again—we wish to restore the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Tang is rising again. Restore the old way.

sentences.zh: 」詔從其請，而謙不奉詔，卒行直帖。

translations.literal: ” The edict accepted their request, but Qian did not obey the edict and ultimately carried out direct posts.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne agreed—but Qian ignored the edict and kept issuing direct orders.

sentences.zh: 又請減百官俸錢，省罷節度觀察判官、推官等員數。

translations.literal: He also requested reducing all officials’ salary money and cutting positions such as military-governor observation commissaries and legal assessors.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to cut every official’s pay and abolish posts such as observation commissaries and legal assessors.

sentences.zh: 以至鄣塞天下山谷徑路，禁止行人，以收商旅征算；

translations.literal: He even blocked mountain paths and roads throughout the realm, forbade travelers, and collected commercial-traveler taxes;
translations.idiomatic: He blocked mountain roads across the empire, barred travelers, and taxed merchants on the move;

sentences.zh: 遣大程官放豬羊柴炭，占庇人戶；

translations.literal: sent great circuit officers to release pigs, sheep, firewood, and charcoal and occupy protected households;
translations.idiomatic: sent circuit officers to monopolize pigs, sheep, firewood, and charcoal and seize protected households;

sentences.zh: 更制括田竿尺；

translations.literal: changed the system of field-survey measuring rods;
translations.idiomatic: changed the rods used to measure fields for taxation;

sentences.zh: 盡率州使公廨錢。

translations.literal: and exhaustively collected prefectural envoys’ office funds.
translations.idiomatic: and drained every prefecture’s envoy office fund.

sentences.zh: 由是天下皆怨苦之。

translations.literal: Because of this the realm all resented and suffered.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 明宗立，下詔暴謙罪，斬於洛市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: When Mingzong ascended he issued an edict exposing Qian’s crimes, executed him in the Luoyang market, and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he published Qian’s crimes, beheaded him in the Luoyang market, and seized his property.

sentences.zh: 遂罷租庸使額，分鹽鐵、度支、戶部為三司。

translations.literal: They then abolished the grain-and-corvée commissioner title and divided Salt Iron, Fiscal Affairs, and Household into three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: They abolished the grain-and-corvée commission and split Salt Iron, Fiscal Affairs, and Household into three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 張延朗

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang

sentences.zh: 張延朗，汴州開封人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang was a native of Kaifeng in Bian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang came from Kaifeng in Bian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事梁，以租庸吏為鄆州糧料使。

translations.literal: He served Liang as a grain-and-corvée clerk and was made Yingzhou grain commissary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as a grain-and-corvée clerk and became Yingzhou grain commissary.

sentences.zh: 明宗克鄆州，得延朗，復以為糧料使，後徙鎮宣武、成德，以為元從孔目官。

translations.literal: When Mingzong captured Yingzhou he got Yanlang and again made him grain commissary; later he was transferred to Xuanyu and Chengde and made original-follower clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took Yingzhou he kept Yanlang as grain commissary. Later, at Xuanyu and Chengde, he made him clerical officer to the original followers.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，為莊宅使、宣徽北院使、忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made palace-estate commissioner, northern Xuanwei commissioner, and military governor of the Zhongwu army.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong’s accession he became palace-estate commissioner, northern Xuanwei commissioner, and military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，拜三司使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing he was appointed three-bureaus commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing 1 he was made three-bureaus commissioner.

sentences.zh: 唐制：戶部度支以本司郎中、侍郎判其事，而有鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Tang system: the Household and Fiscal bureaus had their bureau directors and vice directors judge affairs, and there was a Salt Iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Household and Fiscal affairs were judged by their bureau directors and vice directors, and a Salt Iron transport commissioner stood apart.

sentences.zh: 其後用兵，以國計為重，遂以宰相領其職。

translations.literal: Later, because of military use, national finance became important and a chief minister therefore led the duty.
translations.idiomatic: Later war made state finance paramount, and a chief minister took charge.

sentences.zh: 乾符已後，天下喪亂，國用愈空，始置租庸使，用兵無常，隨時調斂，兵罷則止。

translations.literal: After the Qianfu era the realm fell into chaos and state revenue grew ever emptier; they first set up a grain-and-corvée commissioner. Military use had no fixed pattern—levies came as needed, and when the armies stood down the office stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianfu the realm collapsed and the treasury hollowed out. They created a grain-and-corvée commissioner whose levies rose and fell with war and vanished when the armies rested.

sentences.zh: 梁興，始置租庸使，領天下錢谷，廢鹽鐵、戶部、度支之官。

translations.literal: When Liang rose it first set up a grain-and-corvée commissioner to lead the realm’s finance and abolished the Salt Iron, Household, and Fiscal offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rose it put one grain-and-corvée commissioner over all finance and abolished Salt Iron, Household, and Fiscal.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，因而不改。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and followed without changing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and kept the system.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，誅租庸使孔謙而廢其使職，以大臣一人判戶部、度支、鹽鐵，號曰判三司。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered and took the throne he executed grain-and-corvée commissioner Kong Qian and abolished the commissioner office. He had one great minister judge Household, Fiscal Affairs, and Salt Iron—called judging the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong seized the throne he executed Kong Qian and abolished the grain-and-corvée commission. One great minister then judged Household, Fiscal Affairs, and Salt Iron—the “three bureaus.”

sentences.zh: 延朗因請置三司使，事下中書。

translations.literal: Yanlang therefore requested establishing a three-bureaus commissioner; the matter was sent to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang asked to restore a three-bureaus commissioner, and the matter went to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中書用唐故事，拜延朗特進、工部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，兼判戶部度支事。

translations.literal: The Secretariat used Tang precedent and appointed Yanlang specially advanced and Minister of Works, filled various-circuit salt-and-iron transport commissioner and related posts, and had him concurrently judge Household and Fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat followed Tang precedent and made Yanlang specially advanced and Minister of Works, circuit salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and concurrent judge of Household and Fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔以延朗充三司使，班在宣徽使下。

translations.literal: An edict made Yanlang three-bureaus commissioner, with rank below the Xuanwei commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Yanlang three-bureaus commissioner, ranking below the Xuanwei commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三司置使自此始。

translations.literal: The three-bureaus commissioner office began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The three-bureaus commission began here.

sentences.zh: 延朗號為有心計，以三司為己任，而天下錢谷亦無所建明。

translations.literal: Yanlang was known for having schemes and took the three bureaus as his responsibility, yet the realm’s finance also had nothing he established or clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang was known for cleverness and made the three bureaus his charge, yet he left the realm’s ledgers no clearer than before.

sentences.zh: 明宗常出遊幸，召延朗共食，延朗不至，附使者報曰：「三司事忙，無暇。

translations.literal: Mingzong often went out touring and summoned Yanlang to eat with him; Yanlang did not come and sent word through a messenger: “Three-bureaus affairs are busy—I have no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong often went touring and asked Yanlang to dine with him. Yanlang stayed away and sent word: “The three bureaus are buried in work. I have no time.

sentences.zh: 」聞者笑之。

translations.literal: ” Those who heard laughed at it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Men who heard it laughed.

sentences.zh: 歷泰寧、雄武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He successively served as military governor of the Taining and Xiongwu armies.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded Taining and Xiongwu in turn.

sentences.zh: 廢帝以為吏部尚書兼中書門下平章事，判三司。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor made him Minister of Personnel concurrently Central Secretariat co-equal grand councilor, judging the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor made him Minister of Personnel, co-equal grand councilor, and judge of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖有異志，三司財貨在太原者，延朗悉調取之，高祖深以為恨。

translations.literal: Gaozu of Later Jin harbored ambitions of his own; all the Three Departments’ goods stored at Taiyuan Yanlang requisitioned in full, and Gaozu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Later Jin already nursed designs of his own. Yanlang seized every coin and store the Three Departments had at Taiyuan, and Gaozu never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 晉兵起，廢帝欲親征，而心畏高祖，遲疑不決，延朗與劉延朗等勸帝必行。

translations.literal: When Jin troops rose, the deposed emperor wished to lead the campaign in person but feared Gaozu and hesitated; Yanlang together with Liu Yanlang and others urged the emperor that he must go.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin’s armies rose, the deposed emperor meant to take the field himself—but he feared Gaozu and hung back. Yanlang, Liu Yanlang, and others pressed him to march.

sentences.zh: 延朗籍諸道民為丁及括其馬，丁馬未至，晉兵入京師，高祖得延朗，殺之。

translations.literal: Yanlang registered men from all circuits as conscripts and requisitioned their horses; before the conscripts and horses arrived, Jin troops entered the capital; Gaozu seized Yanlang and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlang drafted men from every circuit and seized their horses. Before either men or mounts arrived, Jin troops were already in the capital. Gaozu took Yanlang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 李嚴，幽州人也，初名讓坤。

translations.literal: Li Yan was a man of Youzhou; his original name was Rangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan came from Youzhou; he was first called Rangkun.

sentences.zh: 事劉守光為刺史，後事莊宗為客省使。

translations.literal: He served Liu Shouguang as regional inspector, later served Zhuangzong as commissioner of the guest bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Shouguang as regional inspector, then Zhuangzong as commissioner of the guest bureau.

sentences.zh: 嚴為人明敏多藝能，習騎射，頗知書而辯。

translations.literal: Yan was bright and quick, skilled in many arts; he practiced mounted archery, knew books well, and was eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and quick, he mastered many crafts, rode and shot well, read widely, and spoke with force.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，使於蜀，為王衍陳唐興復功德之盛，音辭清亮，蜀人聽之皆竦動。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was sent as envoy to Shu; before Wang Yan he set forth the splendor of Tang’s restoration; his voice and words were clear and ringing, and Shu people who heard him were all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 (925) he went to Shu as envoy and before Wang Yan laid out the glory of Tang’s restoration. His voice rang clear; every Shu listener felt a shiver run through him.

sentences.zh: 衍樞密使宋光嗣召嚴置酒，從容問中國事。

translations.literal: Wang Yan’s chief of military affairs Song Guangsi summoned Yan for wine and leisurely asked about affairs in the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan’s chief of military affairs, Song Guangsi, called Yan to wine and, at ease, asked how things stood in the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 嚴對曰：「前年天子建大號於鄴宮，自鄆趨汴，定天下不旬日，而梁之降兵猶三十萬，東漸於海，西極甘涼，北懾幽陵，南逾閩嶺，四方萬里，莫不臣妾。

translations.literal: Yan answered: “Two years ago the Son of Heaven raised the great title at the palace in Ye; from Yan he raced to Bian and settled the realm in less than ten days, and Liang’s surrendered troops still numbered three hundred thousand. East to the sea, west to Gan and Liang, north to You and Ling, south beyond Min Ridge—within ten thousand li on every side, none did not bow as subject.
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered: “Two years ago the Son of Heaven took the great title at Ye. From Yan he drove on Bian and settled the realm in less than ten days—and Liang’s surrendered troops still numbered three hundred thousand. East to the sea, west to Gan and Liang, north to You and Ling, south beyond Min Ridge: for ten thousand li in every direction, all bowed as subjects.

sentences.zh: 而淮南楊氏承累世之強，鳳翔李公恃先朝之舊，皆遣子入侍，稽首稱藩。

translations.literal: Yet the Yang clan of Huainan, inheriting generations of strength, and Lord Li of Fengxiang, relying on ties from the former dynasty, both sent sons to court to serve and bowed as vassals.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangs of Huainan, heirs to generations of power, and Lord Li of Fengxiang, leaning on old ties to the throne, both sent sons to court to serve and bowed as vassals.

sentences.zh: 至荊、湖、吳越，修貢賦，效珍奇，願自比於列郡者，至無虛月。

translations.literal: As for Jing, Hu, Wu, and Yue, they sent tribute and rare goods, seeking to rank themselves with ordinary commanderies—not a month passed without it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Hu, Wu, and Yue sent tribute and curiosities, asking to be counted no more than common prefectures—not a month passed without gifts.

sentences.zh: 天子方懷之以德，而震之以威，天下之勢，不得不一也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven now treats them with virtue and awes them with might—the trend of the realm must inevitably become one.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven now draws them with kindness and shakes them with force. The realm’s drift is toward unity, and nothing can turn it back.

sentences.zh: 」光嗣曰：「荊、湖、吳越非吾所知，若鳳翔則蜀之姻親也，其人反覆，其可信乎？

translations.literal: ” Guangsi said: “Jing, Hu, Wu, and Yue I do not know; but Fengxiang is Shu’s kin by marriage—those people turn and turn again; can they be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: ” Guangsi said: “Jing, Hu, Wu, and Yue I cannot speak for. But Fengxiang is Shu’s kin by marriage—and kin who shift with every wind. Can you trust them?

sentences.zh: 又聞契丹日益強盛，大國其可無慮乎？

translations.literal: I also hear the Khitan grow stronger day by day—can a great state have no concern?
translations.idiomatic: And I hear the Khitan grow stronger every day. Should a great power not worry?

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「契丹之強，孰與偽梁？

translations.literal: ” Yan said: “Which is stronger, the Khitan or the false Liang?
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan said: “Tell me—which is stronger, Khitan or false Liang?

sentences.zh: 」光嗣曰：「比梁差劣爾！

translations.literal: ” Guangsi said: “Compared to Liang they are somewhat weaker!
translations.idiomatic: ” Guangsi said: “A little weaker than Liang, that is all!

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「唐滅梁如拉朽，況其不及乎！

translations.literal: ” Yan said: “Tang destroyed Liang like pulling rotten wood—how much less these!
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan said: “Tang broke Liang like pulling rotten timber. These are less still!

sentences.zh: 唐兵布天下，發一鎮之眾，可以滅虜使無類。

translations.literal: Tang troops fill the realm; mobilize one circuit’s forces and you could wipe out the barbarians without leaving one alive.
translations.idiomatic: Tang soldiers cover the land. Raise one circuit’s host and you could wipe the barbarians from the earth.

sentences.zh: 然而天生四夷，不在九州之內，自前古王者，皆存而不論，蓋不欲窮兵黷武也。

translations.literal: Yet the Four Barbarians were born by Heaven outside the Nine Provinces; from ancient kings onward all left them be and did not speak of conquering them—surely because they wished not to exhaust armies in endless war.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven set the Four Barbarians beyond the Nine Provinces. From the earliest kings, wise rulers let them be and never spoke of finishing them off—because no throne should drown the realm in endless war.

sentences.zh: 」蜀人聞嚴應對，愈益奇之。

translations.literal: Shu people who heard Yan’s replies found him even more extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Shu listeners who heard Yan’s answers thought him stranger and more formidable than before.

sentences.zh: 是時，蜀之君臣皆庸暗，而恃險自安，窮極奢僭。

translations.literal: At that time Shu’s lord and ministers were all mediocre and dim, trusting in natural barriers for security, extravagance pushed to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s court was dull and small-minded, trusting its mountains for safety while luxury ran to excess.

sentences.zh: 嚴自蜀還，具言可取之狀。

translations.literal: When Yan returned from Shu, he fully described how Shu could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan came back from Shu, he laid out in detail how the state could be taken.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗遣嚴以名馬入蜀，市珍奇以充後宮，而蜀法嚴禁以奇貨出劍門，其非奇物而出者，名曰「入草物」，由是嚴無所得而還，惟得金二百兩、地衣、毛布之類。

translations.literal: At first Zhuangzong had sent Yan into Shu with famous horses to buy rare goods for the inner palace; Shu law strictly forbade sending precious goods out through Sword Gate, and whatever was not precious enough to be barred was called “entering-the-grass goods”; thus Yan obtained nothing on the return journey save two hundred taels of gold, moss cloth, and hair-felt and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had first sent Yan into Shu with fine horses to buy treasures for the inner palace. Shu forbade precious goods from passing Sword Gate; anything ordinary enough to leave was called “grass-bound goods.” Yan came back with almost nothing—two hundred taels of gold, moss cloth, hair-felt, and little else.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞之，大怒曰：「物歸中國，謂之『入草』，王衍其能免為『入草人』乎？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard and raged: “Goods returning to the Central Realm are called ‘going into the grass’—can Wang Yan escape becoming a ‘man who goes into the grass’?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heard and raged: “Treasure bound for the Central Realm is ‘going into the grass.’ Can Wang Yan himself escape becoming grass-bound flesh?”

sentences.zh: 」於是決議伐蜀。

translations.literal: ” Thus they resolved to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: ” And so they resolved to march on Shu.

sentences.zh: 冬，魏王繼岌西伐，以嚴為三川招討使，與康延孝以兵五千先行，所過州縣皆迎降。

translations.literal: In winter the Prince of Wei marched west against Shu; Yan was made Three Rivers suppression commissioner and with Kang Yanxiao led five thousand men ahead; every prefecture and county they passed welcomed and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Prince of Wei marched west on Shu. Yan was named Three Rivers suppression commissioner and with Kang Yanxiao took five thousand men ahead. Every prefecture and county they reached opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 延孝至漢州，王衍告曰：「得李嚴來即降。

translations.literal: When Yanxiao reached Han prefecture, Wang Yan sent word: “If Li Yan comes, I will surrender at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanxiao reached Han prefecture, Wang Yan sent word: “Send Li Yan and I surrender at once.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆以伐蜀之謀自嚴始，而衍怨嚴深，不宜往。

translations.literal: ” All said the plan to attack Shu began with Yan, and Yan bore Wang Yan’s deep hatred—not fitting for him to go.
translations.idiomatic: ” Everyone said the war on Shu had begun with Yan, and Wang Yan hated him bitterly—he should not go.

sentences.zh: 嚴聞之喜，即馳騎入益州。

translations.literal: Yan heard and rejoiced, immediately galloped into Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan heard and was glad. He galloped straight into Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 衍見嚴，以妻母為托，即日以蜀降。

translations.literal: Wang Yan met Yan, entrusted wife and mother to him, and that same day Shu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan met Yan, entrusted wife and mother to his care, and that day Shu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 嚴還，明宗以為泗州防禦使，客省使如故。

translations.literal: When Yan returned, Mingzong made him defense commissioner of Sizhou, guest bureau commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan returned, Mingzong made him defense commissioner of Sizhou and kept him as guest bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其後孟知祥屈強於蜀，安重誨稍裁抑之，思有以制知祥者，嚴乃求為西川兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Later Meng Zhixiang grew strong in Shu; An Chonghui gradually curtailed him and sought someone who could control Zhixiang; Yan then asked to be made military inspector of Xichuan horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Later Meng Zhixiang grew bold in Shu. An Chonghui reined him in where he could and looked for a man to hold him in check. Yan asked to be made military inspector of Xichuan horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 將行，其母曰：「汝前啟破蜀之謀，今行，其以死報蜀人矣！

translations.literal: Before he set out his mother said: “You before urged the plan to break Shu; now you go—you will repay Shu with your death!
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, his mother said: “You were the one who opened the road to break Shu. Go now, and Shu will repay you with death.

sentences.zh: 」嚴不聽。

translations.literal: ” Yan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan would not hear her.

sentences.zh: 初，嚴與知祥同事莊宗，時知祥為中門使，嚴嘗有過，莊宗怒甚，命斬之，知祥戒行刑者少緩，入白莊宗曰：「嚴小過，不宜以喜怒殺人，恐失士大夫心。

translations.literal: At first Yan and Zhixiang had served Zhuangzong together; at that time Zhixiang was middle gate attendant; Yan once committed an offense and Zhuangzong was furious, ordered him beheaded; Zhixiang told the executioners to wait a little, entered and told Zhuangzong: “Yan’s fault is small—it is not fitting to kill a man in anger and fear, lest you lose the hearts of the scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yan and Zhixiang had served Zhuangzong together. Zhixiang was then middle gate attendant. Yan once offended, and Zhuangzong in fury ordered his head. Zhixiang told the executioners to hold, went in, and said: “Yan’s fault is small. A ruler should not kill in heat and lose the scholar-officials’ hearts.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗怒稍解，命知祥監笞嚴二十而釋之。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong’s anger eased somewhat; he ordered Zhixiang supervise the beating of Yan twenty strokes and release him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong’s rage cooled. He had Zhixiang oversee twenty strokes and set Yan free.

sentences.zh: 知祥雖與嚴有舊恩，而惡其來。

translations.literal: Though Zhixiang and Yan had old favor between them, he hated Yan’s coming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang owed Yan an old debt of life, but he hated seeing him come.

sentences.zh: 蜀人聞嚴來，亦皆惡之。

translations.literal: Shu people who heard Yan was coming hated him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu heard Yan was coming, the hatred was general.

sentences.zh: 嚴至，知祥置酒從容問嚴曰：「朝廷以公來邪？

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, Zhixiang set wine and at ease asked Yan: “Did the court send you?
translations.idiomatic: Yan arrived. Zhixiang poured wine and asked, calmly: “Did the court send you?

sentences.zh: 公意自欲來邪？

translations.literal: Did you mean to come yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Or did you choose to come yourself?

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「君命也。

translations.literal: ” Yan said: “It was the ruler’s command.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan said: “The ruler’s command.

sentences.zh: 」知祥發怒曰：「天下藩鎮皆無監軍，安得爾獨來此？

translations.literal: ” Zhixiang flew into rage: “Every military governorship in the realm has no military inspector—how can you alone come here?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhixiang erupted: “No frontier post in the realm keeps a military inspector. Why should you alone come here?

sentences.zh: 此乃孺子熒惑朝廷爾！

translations.literal: This is some child beguiling the court!
translations.idiomatic: Some brat has bewitched the throne!

sentences.zh: 」即擒斬之，明宗不能詰也，知祥由此遂反。

translations.literal: ” He seized Yan and executed him; Mingzong could not question it; from this Zhixiang then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: ” He seized Yan and killed him. Mingzong could not call him to account. From that day Zhixiang turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 李仁矩

translations.literal: Li Renju
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju

sentences.zh: 李仁矩，不知其世家。

translations.literal: Li Renju—his family background is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju—nothing is known of his house.

sentences.zh: 少事明宗為客將，明宗即位，以為客省使、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In youth he served Mingzong as guest general; when Mingzong took the throne he was made commissioner of the guest bureau and Left Guard grand general.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served Mingzong as guest general. When Mingzong took the throne he was made commissioner of the guest bureau and Left Guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 明宗祀天南郊，東、西川當進助禮錢，使仁矩趣之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, East and West Circuit were to send aid money for the rites; Renju was sent to hurry them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb, East and West Circuit owed ritual aid money. Renju was sent to collect it.

sentences.zh: 仁矩恃恩驕恣，見藩臣不以禮。

translations.literal: Renju relied on favor and was arrogant and willful; toward frontier lords he showed no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Renju traded on imperial favor and grew proud and reckless. He showed frontier lords no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使董璋置酒召仁矩，仁矩辭醉不往，於傳舍與倡妓飲。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang, military governor of Dongchuan, set wine and summoned Renju; Renju pleaded drunkenness and would not go, drinking instead at the relay station with singing girls.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang, military governor of Dongchuan, sent wine and called Renju in. Renju claimed he was too drunk and stayed away, drinking at the relay station with singing girls instead.

sentences.zh: 璋怒，率衙兵露刃之傳舍，仁矩惶恐，不襪而靴走庭中，璋責之曰：「爾以西川能斬李嚴，謂我獨不能斬爾邪！

translations.literal: Zhang in anger led his guard with naked blades to the relay station; Renju in terror fled into the courtyard booted but without stockings; Zhang rebuked him: “You think because Xichuan could cut down Li Yan, I alone cannot cut you down!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang in fury marched his guard, blades bare, to the relay station. Renju in terror ran into the courtyard in boots but no stockings. Zhang raged at him: “Because Xichuan killed Li Yan, you think I cannot kill you?

sentences.zh: 」顧左右牽出斬之。

translations.literal: ” He looked to his attendants to drag Renju out and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He signaled his men to drag Renju out and take his head.

sentences.zh: 仁矩涕泣拜伏謝罪，乃止。

translations.literal: Renju wept, prostrated himself, and begged forgiveness; only then did Zhang stop.
translations.idiomatic: Renju wept, threw himself down, and begged pardon. Only then did Zhang stay his hand.

sentences.zh: 明日，璋置酒召仁矩，見其妻子，以厚謝之。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang set wine and summoned Renju, showed him his wife and children, and made rich amends.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang called Renju to wine, brought out his wife and children, and made lavish amends.

sentences.zh: 仁矩還，言璋必反。

translations.literal: When Renju returned he said Zhang would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Renju returned he said Zhang would rebel for certain.

sentences.zh: 仁矩素為安重誨所親信，自璋有異志，重誨思有以制之，乃分東川之閬州為保寧軍，以仁矩為節度使，遣姚洪將兵戍之。

translations.literal: Renju had long been trusted by An Chonghui; once Zhang showed signs of disloyalty, Chonghui sought a way to control him and divided Lang prefecture from Dongchuan to form the Baoning army, making Renju its military governor and sending Yao Hong with troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Renju had long stood in An Chonghui’s trust. Once Zhang turned disloyal, Chonghui looked for a way to pin him. He split Lang prefecture from Dongchuan to form the Baoning army, made Renju its military governor, and sent Yao Hong to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 璋以書至京師告其子光業曰：「朝廷割我支郡，分建節髦，又以兵戍之，是將殺我也。

translations.literal: Zhang sent a letter to the capital telling his son Guangye: “The court has cut off my subordinate command and raised a new military governorship, and now garrisons troops against me—this means to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang wrote to the capital and told his son Guangye: “The court has carved away my subordinate command, raised a new military governorship, and posted troops against me. They mean to kill me.

sentences.zh: 若唐復遣一騎入斜谷，吾反必矣！

translations.literal: If Tang sends even one rider into Xiegu Pass, I will rebel!
translations.idiomatic: If Tang sends one more rider through Xiegu Pass, I rebel!

sentences.zh: 與汝自此而決。

translations.literal: From this day I part from you.
translations.idiomatic: After this we are finished.

sentences.zh: 」光業私以書示樞密承旨李虔徽，使白重誨，重誨不省。

translations.literal: Guangye privately showed the letter to chief of military affairs Li Qianhui and had him tell Chonghui; Chonghui paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye quietly showed the letter to chief of military affairs Li Qianhui and had him warn Chonghui. Chonghui ignored it.

sentences.zh: 仁矩至鎮，伺璋動靜必以聞，璋益疑懼，遂決反。

translations.literal: When Renju reached his post he reported Zhang’s every move; Zhang grew more suspicious and afraid, and resolved to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Renju reached his post and reported Zhang’s every move. Zhang grew more afraid and more sure, and chose rebellion.

sentences.zh: 重誨又遣荀咸乂將兵益戍閬州，光業亟言以為不可，重誨不聽。

translations.literal: Chonghui also sent Xun Xianyi with troops to reinforce the garrison at Lang; Guangye urgently said it must not be done, but Chonghui would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui also sent Xun Xianyi with more troops to Lang. Guangye pleaded that it must not be done. Chonghui would not listen.

sentences.zh: 咸乂未至，璋已反，攻閬州，仁矩召將校問策，皆曰：「璋有二心久矣，常以利啖吾兵，兵未可用，而賊鋒方銳，宜堅壁以挫之。

translations.literal: Before Xianyi arrived Zhang had already rebelled and attacked Lang; Renju summoned his officers to ask counsel; all said: “Zhang has had two hearts for long; he often buys our soldiers with profit—the troops cannot be used; the enemy’s edge is sharp—we should hold the walls and blunt them.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xianyi arrived Zhang had rebelled and struck Lang. Renju called his officers for counsel. All said: “Zhang has meant treason for years. He buys our soldiers with silver. The men cannot be trusted, and the enemy’s edge is bright. Hold the walls and wear them down.

sentences.zh: 守旬日，大軍必至，賊當自退。

translations.literal: Hold ten days and the great army will arrive; the enemy will withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hold ten days and the main force will come. The enemy will break on their own.

sentences.zh: 」仁矩曰：「蜀懦，安能當我精銳之師！

translations.literal: ” Renju said: “Shu soldiers are cowards—how can they stand against my crack troops!
translations.idiomatic: ” Renju said: “Shu men are soft. How can they face my picked host?

sentences.zh: 」即驅之出戰，兵未交而潰，仁矩被擒，並其家屬皆見殺。

translations.literal: ” He immediately drove them out to battle; before the lines met they broke and fled; Renju was captured, and his whole household was killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drove them out at once. Before the lines met they collapsed and ran. Renju was taken, and his whole household was killed.

sentences.zh: 毛璋，滄州人也。

translations.literal: Mao Zhang was a man of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁末，戴思遠為橫海軍節度使，璋事思遠為軍校。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Dai Siyuan was military governor of the Henghai army; Zhang served Siyuan as a camp officer.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang’s end Dai Siyuan held Henghai. Zhang served him as a camp officer.

sentences.zh: 晉已下魏博，思遠棄滄州出奔，璋以滄州降晉，以功為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: After Jin took Weibo, Siyuan abandoned Cangzhou and fled; Zhang surrendered Cangzhou to Jin and for merit was made prefect of Bei.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin took Weibo, Siyuan abandoned Cangzhou and fled. Zhang surrendered Cangzhou to Jin and for his deed was made prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 璋為人有膽勇，自晉與梁相拒河上，璋累戰有功。

translations.literal: Zhang was bold and brave; from the time Jin and Liang faced each other on the river Zhang fought repeatedly with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was bold and brave. From the day Jin and Liang faced each other on the river he fought again and again with credit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，拜璋華州節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Zhang was appointed military governor of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong broke Liang, Zhang was made military governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 在鎮多不法，議者疑其有異志，乃徙璋鎮昭義。

translations.literal: At his post he committed many unlawful acts; critics suspected he harbored disloyal intent, and he was transferred to govern Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In office he broke the law often. Critics suspected disloyalty, and he was moved to Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 璋初欲拒命，其判官邊蔚切諫諭之，乃聽命。

translations.literal: At first Zhang wished to refuse the order; his aide Bian Wei urgently remonstrated and persuaded him, and he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhang meant to refuse the transfer. His aide Bian Wei argued him down, and he obeyed.

sentences.zh: 璋累歷藩鎮，又在華州得魏王繼岌伐蜀余貲，既富而驕，益為淫侈。

translations.literal: Zhang had served repeatedly as military governor; at Hua he also obtained the surplus funds from the Prince of Wei’s campaign against Shu; once rich he grew proud and more licentious and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had held one frontier post after another. At Hua he also took the Prince of Wei’s leftover spoils from the Shu campaign. Wealth made him proud, and his excess grew worse.

sentences.zh: 嘗服赭袍飲酒，使其所得蜀奴為王衍宮中之戲於前。

translations.literal: He once wore a vermilion robe while drinking wine and had the Shu slaves he had taken perform the palace entertainments of Wang Yan before him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he drank in a vermilion robe and made his Shu slaves perform Wang Yan’s palace shows before him.

sentences.zh: 明宗聞而惡之，召為金吾上將軍。

translations.literal: Mingzong heard and detested it; he summoned Zhang to be Grand General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong heard and loathed it. He recalled Zhang to be Grand General of the Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 東川董璋上書言璋遣子廷赟持書往西川，疑其有奸。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan memorialized that Zhang had sent his son Tingyun with a letter to Xichuan, suspecting treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang of Dongchuan wrote that Zhang had sent his son Tingyun west to Xichuan with a letter, and suspected treason.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃遣人追還廷赟，並璋下御史獄。

translations.literal: Mingzong then sent men to bring Tingyun back and also cast Zhang into the censor’s prison.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent men to bring Tingyun back and threw Zhang into the censor’s prison.

sentences.zh: 廷赟款稱實璋假子，有叔父在蜀，欲往省之，而無私書。

translations.literal: Tingyun confessed that he was in truth Zhang’s adopted son; he had an uncle in Shu and wished to visit him, and there was no private letter.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun confessed he was Zhang’s adopted son. He had an uncle in Shu and meant only to visit him. There was no secret letter.

sentences.zh: 璋無罪名，有司議：「璋前任藩鎮，陰畜異圖，及處班行，不慎行止。

translations.literal: Zhang had no chargeable crime; the officials deliberated: “In his former military governorship Zhang secretly nourished disloyal designs; in court rank he was careless in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: No crime could be pinned on Zhang. The officials ruled: “As military governor he secretly nursed disloyal designs; in court rank he was careless in conduct.

sentences.zh: 」乃停璋見任官，勒還私第。

translations.literal: ” He was stripped of his current office and ordered back to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was removed from office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 初，廷赟之蜀，與其客趙延祚俱，及召下獄，延祚多捃璋陰事欲言之，璋許延祚重賂以滅口。

translations.literal: At first when Tingyun went to Shu his guest Zhao Yanzuo went with him; when they were summoned and cast into prison Yanzuo gathered many of Zhang’s secret affairs intending to speak of them; Zhang promised Yanzuo a heavy bribe to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingyun first went to Shu his guest Zhao Yanzuo went with him. When both were called in and jailed, Yanzuo collected Zhang’s hidden deeds and meant to speak. Zhang promised him a heavy bribe to stay silent.

sentences.zh: 既出而責賂於璋，不與，延祚乃詣臺自言，並璋復下獄，鞫之無狀。

translations.literal: Once released he demanded the bribe from Zhang; when Zhang would not pay, Yanzuo went to the censorate and spoke on his own; Zhang was cast into prison again; under interrogation no proof was found.
translations.idiomatic: Once free he demanded payment. Zhang refused. Yanzuo went to the censorate on his own and spoke out. Zhang was jailed again. Under questioning nothing held.

sentences.zh: 中丞呂夢奇議曰：「璋前經推劾，已蒙昭雪，而延祚以責賂之故，復加織羅。

translations.literal: Vice censor Lu Mengqi deliberated: “Zhang was already investigated once and cleared; Yanzuo, because the bribe was not paid, has woven new accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Lu Mengqi ruled: “Zhang was tried once and cleared. Yanzuo, denied his bribe, has spun a new net.

sentences.zh: 」乃稍宥璋。

translations.literal: ” Zhang was slightly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang was given a little lenience.

sentences.zh: 璋款上，有告者言夢奇受賂而劾獄不盡，乃移軍巡獄。

translations.literal: Zhang confessed upward; an informer said Mengqi had taken a bribe and had not pursued the case to the end; the case was moved to the military patrol prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang petitioned from below. An informer said Mengqi had taken a bribe and stopped the inquiry short. The case went to the military patrol prison.

sentences.zh: 獄吏希旨，鍛煉其事，璋具伏：許賂延祚而未與，嘗以馬借夢奇而無受賂。

translations.literal: The prison clerks followed the desired verdict and forged the matter; Zhang fully confessed: he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but not paid it; he had once lent Mengqi a horse but had taken no bribe.
translations.idiomatic: The jail clerks shaped the case to order. Zhang confessed everything: he had promised Yanzuo a bribe and never paid; he had lent Mengqi a horse, but taken no bribe.

sentences.zh: 璋坐長流儒州，已而令所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: Zhang was sentenced to long exile in Ruzhou; shortly afterward he was ordered to take his own life wherever he was.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was sentenced to lifelong exile in Ruzhou. Before long the order came that he should take his own life wherever he stood.
